output.summary: The yield fall is real: the CMM gauge R&R and program are unchanged, and Halvard's PPM rose. The new-operator cohort is ruled out, because their reject rate matches experienced operators and the decline began before they ran alone. Fatigue, Corvane hardness spread and spindle wear are all confounded. Lot order, the service deferral and the 12-hour shifts all moved together in time, and scrap-tag times are batch-written, so they say nothing about the hour of machining. Backlog pressure clearly caused the service deferrals. Evidence is insufficient to commit to a single root cause. The best step is a cheap, reversible staggered service plus a Tamsworth bar trial, with cycle-counter matching and the Line 6 CMM data. Reverting shifts, permanently dropping Corvane, punishing operators and sampling inspection are premature or harmful.
